To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the awarding of government contracts to private firms is associated with political donations from firm owners and executives and that the association varies across three separate phases of the public-private contract process.

(1) the awarding of construction contracts is associated with a spike in campaign contributions from construction firm owners and managers, (2) the spike is comparable in size to the election cycle premium, and (3) the spike occurs in the months before the award is made.
political donations by construction firms are associated with the timing of public construction contracts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between political donations and public-private contracting.
the relationship between public policy decisions and the political contributions of the private firms involved.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
public-private contract recipients are more likely to give money to politicians in the months before and during the contract award process.

the results of this research indicate that political giving by construction firm owners is not simply a matter of political contributions being made to obtain public contracts, but rather a complex dynamic of reciprocity and exchange between public and private actors.
public-private contract awarding is a political process, and that political reciprocity is an important component of that process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
public-private contracting is not only about economic outcomes, but also about political outcomes.
public-private contract awards are not only associated with political contributions, but that these contributions are strategic, with timing and amounts varying across the procurement process.
political reciprocity exists in the award of public-private contracts, and that this reciprocity can be measured in a way that is useful for policy makers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
public-private contracting and political giving are linked in a reciprocal exchange, and that the dynamics of this exchange are not well-understood.
public-private contracting is a two-way street, and that the political benefits of winning contracts are substantial.
the political donations of public-private contractors are strategic and that they are not simply a product of the political leanings of the firms.
